text: The Titanic lies about three thousand eight hundred metres down, at the bottom of the North Atlantic. Every ten metres of seawater adds about one more atmosphere of pressure. So down there, it's around three hundred and eighty times the pressure at the surface. That's almost four hundred kilograms pressing on every square centimetre. Like a grand piano, balanced on your fingertip. Anything hollow down there is being squeezed from every direction at once. Send an empty soda can down there, and it wouldn't just dent. It would be crushed flat, long before it reached the bottom.
